p: Babylon is taken: After God had used the Babylonian's service to punish other nations, this shows that their turn will come to be punished.
Merodach is broken in pieces: These were two of their chief idols.
there cometh a nation against her: That is, the Medes and the Persians.
come: When Cyrus will take Babel.
weeping: Read Jer 31:9.
shepherds have caused them to go: Their governors and ministers by their examples have provoked them to idolatry.
mountain to hill: They have committed idolatry in every place.
the habitation of justice: For the Lord dwelt among them in his temple and would have maintained them by his justice against their enemies.
Flee out of the midst of: When God will deliver you by Cyrus.
before the flocks: That is, most forward and without fear.
shall be satisfied: Shall be made rich by it.
and bellow as bulls: For joy of the victory that you had against my people.
and hiss at all her plagues: In sign of contempt and disdain.
Put yourselves in array against Babylon: He speaks to the enemies the Medes and Persians.

sinned against the LORD: Though the Lord called the Babylonians his servants and their work his work in punishing his people, yet because they did it not to glorify God, but for their own malice and to profit themselves, it is here called sin.
sower from Babylon: Destroy her so that no one is left to work the ground or to take the fruit of it.
Assyria hath devoured him: Meaning Tiglath-pilesar who carried away the ten tribes.
bones: He carried away the rest, that is Judah and Benjamin.
Merathaim: That is, Babylon: thus the Lord raised up Cyrus.
hammer of the whole earth cut: Nebuchadnezzar, who had smitten down all the princes and people of the world.
bulls: Her princes and mighty men.
flee and escape from the land: Of the Jews who would be delivered by Cyrus.
and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon: He shows that when God executes his judgments against his enemies, that his Church will then have rest.

drought is upon her waters: For Cyrus cut the river Euphrates and divided the course of it into many streams, so that it might be passed over as though there had been no water: which he did by the counsel of two of Belshazzar's captains, who conspired against their king, because he had gelded one of them in spite and slain the son of the other.
wild beasts of the desert with: Read Isa 13:21.
the ends of the earth: Meaning, that the Persians would gather their army from many nations.
became feeble: Which is meant of Belshazzar, Dan 5:6.
shepherd that will stand before me: Read Geneva "Jer 49:19"
